keyQuestions.text: Human surface, phases 001-activity-and-actor and 002-routine-layer: which reference files implement an activity feed, an inbox, an actor on a record and routines with an until outcome, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which failures or fixes in those repos does the plan not guard against?

Prompt and records, phases 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 009-skills and 010-conversations: which reference files implement a working place named in the prompt, shared and per-bot memory with a size bound, a skill list under a cap and an append-only conversation with bot routing, and which pitfalls did those repos hit?

resolvedQuestions.text: Human surface, phases 001-activity-and-actor and 002-routine-layer: which reference files implement an activity feed, an inbox, an actor on a record and routines with an until outcome, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which failures or fixes in those repos does the plan not guard against?

Prompt and records, phases 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 009-skills and 010-conversations: which reference files implement a working place named in the prompt, shared and per-bot memory with a size bound, a skill list under a cap and an append-only conversation with bot routing, and which pitfalls did those repos hit?

keyFindings.text: **Phase 001 — `stopped` is a derived predicate over a stop instant, not a status value.** The reference never stores a "stopped" status: `stoppedByYou` returns `task?.status === "failed" && Boolean(task.stoppedAt)` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/tasks/queries.ts:300-304], and `taskGroup` routes a failed task to `stopped` or `failed` on that predicate alone [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:82-87]. The 003 synthesis already carries the gap that `stopped` has no data source (003-plan-depth-research §4.001 gap 1); what is new is the shape of the fix — one nullable `stoppedAt` instant on the run record plus a predicate, so no new status value, no index column and no `SCHEMA_VERSION` move, which is exactly the constraint 001's own risk table imposes. (observed for the reference; inferred for the plan's fix shape)

**Phase 001 — the reference dedupes a needs-you item against the run that raised it, and the plan does not.** `groupActivity` skips an approval or question whose `channelId` is one of the listed task's conversations, so it is shown once, as the task [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:147-152]. Phase 001 sources `needs_you` from the status index and `working` from the bot's held lease side file [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:143], and a parked run holds its lease while its item is open, so one parked run prints twice: once under `needs_you` and once under `working`. The plan needs one dedupe rule keyed on the item's `runId`, which REQ-003 already carries. (observed for the reference; inferred for the plan's absence)

**Phase 001 — the reference drops an action's first row when its failure row is loaded beside it, and the plan has no retry rule.** `oneRowPerAction` collects the `attempt` ids of failed, stopped and refused actions and filters out the matching `computer.action_allowed` row, because "the first is the one a reader believes" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/activity-rows.ts:70-96]. The runtime's queue retries a claimed request up to three times, so one request can leave more than one run record, and `bots activity` has no rule for which of them it prints. The reference's rule is the liftable one: the terminal row wins and the earlier row is left out of the read, not out of the trail. (observed)

**Phase 001 — the seven group titles are liftable verbatim and the plan fixes only the ids.** `ACTIVITY_GROUPS` declares each group as `{ id, title }` in one ordered array: `needs_you`/"Needs you", `working`/"Working", `scheduled`/"Scheduled", `done`/"Done", `stopped`/"Stopped", `failed`/"Failed", `recurring`/"Recurring" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:28-39]. Phase 001's REQ-001 fixes the seven ids and their order and REQ-002 requires each group to carry a `title`, but no line in the phase fixes the title strings, so a builder invents seven labels that the screen's sample payload then has to match. Lift the array as-is under the MIT notice REQ-006 already requires. (observed)

**Phase 002 — the plan sorts `recurring` by next fire and the reference deliberately does not.** Phase 001's REQ-002 requires rows "soonest first in `scheduled` and `recurring`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:118]. The reference sorts `scheduled` ascending by time and never sorts `recurring`: it appends routines, then goals, then check-ins in insertion order [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:175-192]. The evidence supports the plan for a terminal list, where a next-fire column is the useful ordering, but the reference's reason is worth keeping: a time-sorted recurring list reorders itself on every poll, so a row moves under the reader's cursor. State the sort and accept the movement, or keep insertion order and print the next fire as a column. (observed)

**Phase 002 — the reference frames a firing in three sentences because a live firing read its own instruction as a routine-management question, did nothing, and recorded `succeeded`.** `FIRING_FRAME` is three fixed sentences: that this is a scheduled firing happening now, that the work belongs in this turn, and that managing routines is not what was asked [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/routine-firing.ts:9-13]. The comment records the failure verbatim: the instruction "Every run, append the current date and time …" was sent as the turn's user message, the model called `list_routines`, found a routine that already said that, answered that it was already configured, and appended nothing — "a routine telling somebody it is working while doing nothing at all, which is worse than one that breaks" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/routine-firing.ts:18-34]. Phase 002 changes when a bot runs and when it stops and never what the run is told: a search of its spec for `firing`, `frame` or `prompt` finds no framing rule. This is the highest-value lift in the phase, it is MIT, and the plan does not guard against the failure at all. (observed)

**Phase 002 — the reference records a second live failure on the identity of a "tell" routine, and the plan's `does: tell` has no identity rule.** `checkInSubject` falls back to the instruction collapsed to one line and cut to 120 units, and the comment records why: a check-in with no Name went in with an empty subject, the server counts a check-in with no link and the same subject as the same one, so every unnamed "Only tell you" landed on the bot's default check-in and was refused as already there [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/routines/plan.ts:52-68]. Phase 002 maps `does: tell` to local-only delivery [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:114] and states no identity for a tell routine, so two tell routines with the same body either collide or duplicate. (observed)

**Phase 005 — the reference bounds on read, the plan bounds only on write, and the plan admits a state it gives no exit from.** `load()` filters and then `.slice(0, LIMITS.records)`, so a file that is already over the bound still renders [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/memory.js:37] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/memory.js:11]. Phase 005 refuses an append that would pass the bound [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:150] and REQ-016 states that two concurrent appends can both pass the count check and leave the file one line over [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:168]. After that race every later append is refused and no line names the repair; `--forget` is the exit but nothing says so. The reference's read-side bound is the missing half: render what is there, refuse only the growth. (observed)

**Phase 005 — the reference degrades a prompt that is over budget in three steps and the plan refuses instead, so a bot at both caps can never run.** `render` drops whole lines from the last section that has lines, re-composing and re-measuring after each drop; when no lines remain it shortens the last prose section by exactly the overflow in characters, with an ellipsis; and a shortened section that would fall below `MIN_PROSE_CHARS = 40` is removed rather than kept as a stub, so an empty document always fits [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinymemory/crates/tinymemory-tools/src/recall/render.rs:80-116] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinymemory/crates/tinymemory-tools/src/recall/render.rs:22]. Phase 005's REQ-015 gives the conversation block way first and then refuses the run `prompt-over-budget`, and phase 009 states the consequence plainly: two full memory files and a full skills list are 27,680 bytes before any wrapper, so a bot at both caps is always refused [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:162]. The evidence supports the plan's refusal for authored blocks — a truncated `SKILL.md` is a half instruction — and supports the reference's ladder for the conversation block, which is the one block the plan already lets give way. The missing piece is the reference's floor rule: a block that would survive only as a stub is dropped, not kept. (observed)

**Phase 005 — the reference uses one unit for every budget and stores the measured figure on the compiled document; the plan mixes bytes and characters.** `estimate_tokens` is `text.chars().count().div_ceil(CHARS_PER_TOKEN)` with four characters per token, "the estimate every context budget uses" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinymemory/crates/tinymemory-tools/src/recall/render.rs:29-31], and `ContextDoc` carries `tokens` beside `markdown` so a caller checks the budget without re-measuring [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinymemory/crates/tinymemory-tools/src/context/compile/mod.rs:34-46]. The 003 synthesis already carries the plan's unit mixing as 005 gap 5 (bytes for memory and skills, characters for the transcript and the total); what is new is the reference's fix — one unit, one estimator, and the measured figure stored on the document rather than recomputed by each reader. (observed for the reference; the plan's mixing is carried by 003-plan-depth-research §4.005 gap 5)

**Phase 009 — the reference never loads every skill body; it lists names and descriptions and loads one body on mention, which removes the cap problem the plan refuses at.** `lines()` renders one `- <name>: <description>` line per skill for the agent [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/skills.js:76-78], `mentions()` finds `/name` in a message and returns only names that resolve [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/skills.js:58-62], and `content()` loads one skill's body only when it is used [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/skills.js:81-96]. Phase 009 measured the sixteen `SKILL.md` files at 219,862 bytes and answered with two byte caps that refuse [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:93] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:162]. The reference's two-tier design is the alternative the plan did not weigh: a list always fits where the bodies do not, and a body is paid for only when a run uses it. The evidence supports adding the list tier; it does not support dropping the caps, which still bound the one body a run loads. (observed)

**Phase 009 — the reference's skill block carries the skill's directory, its compatibility line and its resource files; the plan's block is the body alone.** `content()` emits `<skill_content name="…">`, the body, `Skill directory: <dir>`, the line "Relative paths in this skill are relative to the skill directory", an optional `It says it needs: <compatibility>` line, and a `<skill_resources>` list of the skill's files [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/skills.js:81-96]. Phase 009's REQ-002 inserts the body inside one `<skill_content name="<name>">` block per skill and names no directory line and no resource list [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/009-skills/spec.md:161], so a skill whose body says "run scripts/foo.sh" has no anchor and no statement of what it ships. (observed)

**Phase 010 — the deferred conversation rotation has a named reference, and its soft-threshold-with-one-advisory rule is the part to lift first.** `CompactionPolicy` compacts above a hard ceiling of `min(0.95, auto_compact_pct + 0.10)` of the context window, or above the soft threshold once the model has already received its one wind-down advisory, and end-of-turn callers use `over_soft` directly because there is no further cooperative turn to wait for [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/turnstone-main/turnstone/core/compaction.py:47-68]. `calibrated_chars_per_token` anchors the chars-per-token ratio to the provider's own reported count, subtracting fixed charges first and refusing to calibrate from a request that replays a native lane [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/turnstone-main/turnstone/core/compaction.py:96-120]. Phase 010 defers rotation by decision, which the 003 synthesis already records as 010 gap 7; what is new is that the deferral now has a reference to lift, and that the reference's cheapest half is the policy object, not the summarizer. (observed for the reference; the deferral is carried by 003-plan-depth-research §4.010 gap 7)

**The reference filters control characters out of drawn text; the plan replaces each with `?`, and the plan's side is the better one.** `safe_text` keeps every character that is not a control character and keeps `\n` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/theme.rs:88-93]. Phase 003's `theme::printable` replaces each control character with `?` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/003-shell-and-navigation/spec.md:150]. A filter makes a corrupted string look clean and hides that anything was removed; a replacement shows the reader that a byte was there. The evidence supports the plan, and the reference is the counter-example worth citing in the phase so a builder does not "simplify" to a filter. (observed)

**The reference stamps every transcript entry with a monotonic revision so the renderer can skip what did not change; the plan's only draw optimisation is row windowing.** `Entry` carries a `revision: u64` taken from a process-wide `AtomicU64` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/state.rs:21-24] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/state.rs:45-51]. Phase 003's `004-panes` child tests "a 2,000-row draw that visits only the rows its body holds", which bounds the work by the visible window and not by what changed [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/004-panes/spec.md:3]. The two are complementary: windowing bounds the rows visited, a revision bounds the cells redrawn inside them. (observed)

**The reference's four tabs are a closed cycle with `ALL`, `title`, `next` and `previous`, and its order is declared part of the CLI UX contract; the plan's key map has six exclusive contexts and no cycle.** `AppTab` is `Logs`, `Chat`, `Config`, `Settings`, with `ALL: [Self; 4]`, `title()`, and `next`/`previous` wrapping by modulo [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/ui_state.rs:8-36]. Phase 003's key map has six exclusive contexts and binds typing only in the overlay and palette contexts [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/003-plan-depth-research/research/research.md:181-196]. The reference's cycle is the cheaper model and the plan's contexts are the more precise one; the evidence supports keeping the plan's contexts and adding the reference's `ALL`-array-plus-`next` shape so the tab order has one declaration rather than one per key binding. (observed)

**The reference's status vocabulary has six values and distinguishes cancelled from failed and stale from unknown; the plan's seven activity groups fold both away.** `Status` is `Running`, `Success`, `Error`, `Waiting`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, each with a `label()` and a `marker()`: running/"·", done/"✓", failed/"✗", needs input/"!", cancelled/"–", stale/"?", where `Unknown` is labelled "stale" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/activity.rs:5-35]. Phase 001's seven groups are `needs_you`, `working`, `scheduled`, `done`, `stopped`, `failed`, `recurring` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:112], so a cancelled run has no group of its own and a stale read has no marker at all. The reference's `stale` is the one worth adding: it is the state a screen shows when its data is older than the runtime, which is exactly what phase 001's refresh-on-read can fail to do. (observed)

**The reference's transcript reducer ignores events for another `client_id`, so one process-wide broadcast bus can be drained safely — the guard a multi-bot screen needs.** `TranscriptState::apply_event` folds a typed `WebChannelEvent` into the transcript and "events for a different `client_id` are ignored, so a process-wide broadcast bus can be drained safely" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/state.rs:1-12]. Phase 003's `002-architecture-and-contracts` child creates an event source and a pure reducer but states no filter for an event that belongs to another bot or another run [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/002-architecture-and-contracts/spec.md:60]. A screen that draws several bots from one bus needs that filter, and the reference's rule is one line. (observed)

**The topic's premise is half wrong, and the correction matters for every later iteration: `openhuman-main`'s `vendor/` holds 21 empty directories, and the `openhuman-tui` source is byte-identical in both checkouts.** `diff -rq openhuman-main/crates openhuman-full/crates` prints nothing, and `diff -rq openhuman-main/crates/openhuman-tui openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui` prints nothing, so the TUI crate is the same 53 files and 9,601 lines in both. What `openhuman-full` adds is the vendored crate *sources*: every one of `openhuman-main/vendor/*` holds 0 files, while `openhuman-full/vendor/*` holds the real crates [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full.build.log:950] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full.build.log:956]. The build log proves `openhuman-tui v0.64.20` compiled in `openhuman-full` in 4m 33s, so "built" is true as a build event and false as a source difference. The 001 synthesis's claim that openhuman "ships the only full terminal client" stands; the claim that the full checkout adds a TUI does not. (observed)

**OpenGhost's rules engine carries a per-moment capability matrix and an explicit list of the moments it cannot honour, and the deferred per-action packet has neither.** `CAN` maps each of the 17 moments to the actions a rule may take there — `PreToolUse` allows `deny, ask, allow, context, check, notify, log, stop` while `PermissionRequest` allows only `allow, deny, notify, log` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/rules.js:44-50], and `FOREIGN_EVENTS` names the 16 Claude Code moments the app has no counterpart for, with the rule that such a hook "is brought over only by adapting it" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenGhost-main/rules.js:39-40]. The 001 synthesis already names `rules.js` as the liftable layer for a later packet [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:93]; what is new is that the matrix and the foreign list are the two parts that make the engine safe, and neither is in the plan. (observed for the reference; the lift is carried by the 001 synthesis)

**The 001 synthesis's reuse table mis-cites the action-kind classifier, and a builder following it would lift the wrong file.** `shared/tool-name.ts` humanises a tool name for display: `readToolName` returns a `{ label, detail }` pair, `wholeToolName` resolves a shortened name, and `knowShortenedToolNames` learns what a hash stands for, because "the model is offered `mcp__notes__search_notes` … none of that is the reader's problem" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/tool-name.ts:15-59]. The action-kind classifier is `app/src/lib/approvals.ts`: `ActionKind` at line 62, `ActionKindPolicy` at line 71, `ConversationGrant` at line 76, `RuleBehaviour` at line 60 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/approvals.ts:54-100], with the recognition rules written as a table in `docs/approvals.md` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/docs/approvals.md:34-45]. The 001 synthesis's row "Action-kind classifier | OpenBot `shared/tool-name.ts` | MIT | Approval ladder" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:139] should read `app/src/lib/approvals.ts` plus `docs/approvals.md`. (observed)

**The reference has a third answer — hand the action to the person — and phase 006's `once|deny` scope cannot express it.** `RuleBehaviour` is `"allow" | "pre_approved" | "ask" | "hand_off"` and `ActionKindPolicy` is `"open" | "ask" | "hand_off"` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/approvals.ts:60-71], and `HostCommandPolicy` is a separate `"ask" | "allow" | "never"` for host commands [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/approvals.ts:87]. Phase 006's scope is `once|deny` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:43]. `hand_off` is not a denial and not an allow: the bot stops and the person does the step, which is exactly the passkey and phone-code case the 001 synthesis describes for the computer. A `hand_off` scope is the cheapest way to represent it without building the executor-side policy. (observed)

**The reference lets a kind of action be opened only by an allow given on that kind's own card, and phase 006's ladder has no such rule.** "An allow reaches a kind of action only when it was given on that kind's card. 'Always allow here' on an ordinary click on a site does not let the Bot press that site's Send or Place your order button, and a rule you type in Settings, or a team rule, doesn't open a kind either. A rule that asks or hands off always applies." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/docs/approvals.md:29-32]. Phase 006 writes the ladder as a doc and applies rung 1 at the needs-you gate [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:40], and that doc does not exist yet — `.skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/bots-run/references/` holds `run-queue-and-answer.md` and no `approval-ladder.md` — so the rule has nowhere to land. It is the one rung-1 rule that stops a broad allow from silently opening a payment, and it belongs in the doc verbatim. (observed)

**The reference's conversation grant is keyed on four things — the same bot, tool, place and account — and phase 006's grant is keyed on four different ones.** "Allow for this conversation … the same Bot, the same tool, the same place and the same account. It doesn't reach another conversation, another Bot or another tool." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/docs/approvals.md:22], with the type at [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/approvals.ts:76]. Phase 006's grant carries "the action kind, the action in the bot's words, the rung that made it ask and the scope the answer granted" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:50]. The plan's grant records *why* it asked and the reference's records *what it covers*; a grant that does not name the place and the account cannot be checked against the next call, so the plan's grant is a record and the reference's is a key. (observed)

**The reference's per-bot app refusal carries four reasons and a marker, and it treats a recorded posture as a hint rather than the state.** `CONNECT_APP_MARKER = "[connect-app]"` prefixes a machine-readable refusal so the transcript can draw the app card in place, and the file exists because "a wording that lives in two files is a contract that drifts" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/connect-prompt.ts:1-19]. `ConnectReason` is `"connect" | "reconnect" | "shared" | "access"` — no account, a withdrawn grant, a shared team account nobody connected, and a plain not-granted [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/connect-prompt.ts:21-35] — and the card "asks the server for the app's state for this person and this Bot when it is drawn, and draws that", with the hint winning only where the live state is stale [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/connect-prompt.ts:30-33]. Phase 007 has one refusal, `apps-unknown-server`, and records `HonoredPosture.apps` as the truth of what was honored [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:30]. The four reasons are the taxonomy a per-bot app layer needs, and the hint-not-state rule is the one that keeps a recorded posture from being read as a live grant. (observed)

**The lifted matcher carries a cost model and a hard state cap, and the plan's "lifted with its notice" line states neither.** `createSecretMatcher` scans each value in turn until the scans have cost about what building the one-pass matcher would — `BUILD_COST = 8`, "building costs about a Map write per code unit of the values, a scan a compare" — and only then builds the Aho–Corasick index [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts:23-53]. The index itself is capped at `MAX_SECRET_MATCHER_STATES = 1_000_000`, past which it falls back to the per-value scan, because "very long values (keys of thousands of characters, each in several encodings) could push past what a Map holds" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts:16-21]. Phase 008 says the module is "rakazo's one-pass multi-value matcher, lifted with its notice and a statement of changes" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:119]. A builder who reimplements the matcher from its description will build the index unconditionally and can exhaust memory on a long key; the two constants are the part that makes the lift safe. (observed)

**The matcher returns merged ranges, not matches, and that is what stops a redactor leaving half a secret behind.** `ranges(text)` returns "the stretches values cover, in order, as [start, end); overlapping matches make one stretch" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts:5-12]. Phase 008's `leak-checks.md` holds "every check" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:55] and the plan names no rule for two secrets that overlap in one text. A redactor that replaces each match in turn leaves the tail of the longer secret in place when a shorter one sits inside it; the reference's merged-stretch return is the fix and it is one line of the lifted contract. (observed)

**The placeholder guard works by holding the known placeholder values and refusing a non-development environment that still carries one, and the plan's `bots secret set` has no such refusal.** `DEDICATED_SECRET_PLACEHOLDERS` is a `Set` of the dev and example values, `isDevSecretAllowed` gates on `RAKAZO_ALLOW_DEV_SECRETS`, `VITEST` and `NODE_ENV`, and `resolveAuthSecret` throws `RUNTIME_SECRETS_ERROR` when a non-dev environment holds `DEV_AUTH_SECRET_PLACEHOLDER` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/node/secrets-guard.ts:1-55].
